sections.title: Wardrobe map (§21, §14A) — one outfit per story day
sections.md:
**Why v2 (the user, 2026-09-29):** "the wardrobe map is just the same wardrobe all over even though its a different day/event". v1 put every problem beat in P-D1 and every after beat in P-D2 — two outfits for 21 beats across nine years and six weeks. v2 derives a story day per event (§14A D1–D4) and gives each its own outfit. **Novelty (§14A):** 16 body story days for P. Consecutive days change ≥2 layers including BASE; no BASE class twice in an act; no exact garment twice; colour family rotates (audited in `work/wardrobe.py`). Signature item (declared, §14A): her reading glasses on a thin beaded cord round her neck. Problem days (Acts 1–2) muted, cool-season indoors; after days (Acts 3–5) carry colour, late spring (§30F). Never her sheet outfit (duck-egg jumper, check skirt). The LOWER layer decides the product's visibility and is never modified to expose it — the one roll (BR-17a) is her rolling the trouser leg to put the strap on, and it falls in BR-17b. The strap is worn on bare skin on every worn beat. Hooks keep P-D1 / P-D2 (their renders are confirmed); the doctor keeps D-D1 (one consulting-room session, TH-locked).
